newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC issues warning to Carlton.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC issues warning to Carlton.

text.p: Britain's Independent Television Commission on Wednesday said it issued a formal warning to Carlton Television over an "acquaintance rape" scene in the programme "London Bridge".

The ITC said it issued the warning after concluding that the episode of "London Bridge" was "in serious breach of the ITC Programme Code." It was the first time that the ITC had imposed a formal warning on Carlton Television.
Carlton Television, a unit of Carlton Communications Plc, broadcast the episode at 10:45 p.m. on April 18. The programme showed a man having forcible sexual intercourse with a drunken woman.
The ITC said the scene was "unacceptably extended and excessively detailed in terms of its depiction of the process of rape, step by step from beginning to end.

The ITC said it noted that the programme had been subject to Carlton's own strict compliance procedure, and it noted Carlton's good record over the years in portraying violence and sex. "However, the commission concluded that in respect of both length and detail the sequence went beyond acceptable boundaries even for an adult drama broadcast late in the evening."
